newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends softer as U.S. dollar rises.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends softer as U.S. dollar rises.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended softer on Tuesday at C$1.3878 (US$0.7205) from Monday's close of C$1.3869 (US$0.7210), left behind by a rising U.S. dollar, dealers said. * They said the Canadian dollar weakened in quiet trading as the U.S. dollar gained under power from U.S. stocks, which ended the day higher.
"It's been one of the quietest days we've had in six months," the currency trader said.

Analysts said underlying weakness for the Canadian dollar continued to arise from speculation about whether the Federal Reserve would raise rates and if the Bank of Canada would attempt to resist the growing pressure to follow the Fed.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar edged up to 1.2347 marks compared to Monday's close of 1.2342 marks and firmed to 90.92 from Monday's 90.54 yen.
